data.name: Andorra
data.region: Southern Europe (Pyrenees), not an EU member (monetary agreement, uses EUR)
data.summary: Personal income tax (IRPF) at a maximum 10%. Gains on listed or unlisted shares are exempt unless the seller (with family) held more than 25% in the prior 12 months, and even then exempt after 10 years of ownership; gains on investment fund units are exempt. Dividends from Andorran companies are exempt; foreign dividends are taxed at 10% with credit for foreign withholding (first EUR 3,000 of savings income exempt). No inheritance, gift or wealth tax. Andorran real estate gains fall under a separate real estate capital gains tax (1%-15%); foreign real estate gains are exempt after 10 years.

regimes.name: Ordinary tax residence
regimes.description: IRPF (Llei 5/2014) on worldwide income: general rate 10%, with a 5% effective rate on the EUR 24,000-40,000 band delivered via a credit. Savings income base reduced by a EUR 3,000 allowance.
regimes.eligibility: Tax resident if living in Andorra more than 183 days in the calendar year, or if the main centre of economic activities or interests is in Andorra, directly or indirectly. Requires an Andorran residence permit (see residency).

capital_gains.summary: Gains on shares (listed or unlisted, Andorran or foreign) are exempt if the seller, together with related persons and family up to the third degree, did not hold more than 25% of the company in the 12 months before the sale; larger holdings are also exempt if owned for at least 10 years. Gains on units of any collective investment undertaking are exempt. Exemption excluded for shares of companies whose assets are 50%+ Andorran real estate. Taxable gains (e.g. a >25% stake held under 10 years, bonds) are taxed at up to 10%. Foreign real estate gains exempt after 10 years of ownership. Andorran real estate gains are subject to the separate Impost sobre les plusvàlues (1%-15%, rate depending on holding period), not IRPF.
capital_gains.exemptions_thresholds: Holding <= 25% (12-month look-back, family aggregated): exempt. >25% held 10+ years: exempt. Funds: exempt. Foreign real estate held 10+ years: exempt. Andorran real estate held over 10 years: not integrated in the IRPF base.
capital_gains.important_exceptions: Shares in Andorran property-rich companies (>=50% Andorran real estate) excluded from the exemption.

open_questions: Guide is the 2025 edition; no 2026 change to these exemptions found, but 2026 edition not checked.

capital_gains.rate_basis: Portfolio holdings (<25%) exempt. private_business_sale 0 assumes a >25% stake held 10+ years (10% if held less than 10 years). Foreign real estate 0 after 10 years (10% otherwise). Andorran real estate: separate plusvàlua tax, rate not verified for long holdings.
capital_gains.professional_trader: Exemption applies to transfers of shares regardless of frequency per the guide; trading as a business activity would be business income at 10%.
capital_gains.holding_period_rules: 10 years for >25% stakes and for foreign real estate.
capital_gains.foreign_assets: Same exemptions for foreign shares and funds.

dividends.summary: Dividends from Andorran-resident companies (and Andorran funds) subject to Andorran corporate tax are exempt. Foreign dividends are taxable at 10% as savings income, with a deduction for international double taxation; the first EUR 3,000 of savings income is exempt. Withholding of 10% applies at Andorran banks by default.
dividends.rate_basis: General IRPF rate 10% on foreign dividends; with typical 15% treaty WHT the credit (capped at Andorran tax) eliminates the Andorran tax, though Andorra has few treaties so non-treaty WHT often applies.
dividends.withholding_outbound: Not researched (dividends paid to non-residents fall under the non-resident income tax).
dividends.treaty_network: Small treaty network (around a dozen, mainly European: France, Spain, Portugal, Luxembourg, UAE etc.); no treaty with the US (count and list not verified).

wealth_tax.summary: No net wealth tax and no levy on financial assets. Communes levy small property-related taxes; a vacant-dwelling tax of EUR 5.05/m2 applies to homes empty over 2 years.
open_questions: No official page explicitly states 'no wealth tax'; none is listed among state or communal taxes.
wealth_tax.property_tax_note: Communal property tax (low); vacant dwellings tax EUR 5.05/m2. Property transfer tax (ITP) 4% on purchases.

inheritance.summary: No inheritance or gift tax. Inheritances and donations are outside the IRPF; gains revealed on transfer at death are exempt; gifts of real estate between relatives up to the third degree are exempt from the real estate capital gains tax, and transfers of shares among relatives up to the third degree are exempt from the 4% ITP.

income.name: Andorra

income_tax.summary: IRPF is a flat 10% on the general base after a EUR 24,000 personal minimum, minus a bonus of 50% of the tax on that base capped at EUR 800, so the effective marginal rates are 0% to EUR 24,000, 5% from EUR 24,000 to 40,000 and 10% above. Employees pay 6.5% CASS (pensions 3.5% + general 3%); the self-employed 22% of a chosen base, ceiling EUR 3,674.72 a month.

employment_deduction.note: Deemed 'other expenses' of 3% of gross wages, maximum EUR 2,500 (Govern d'Andorra IRPF guide, section 6.2).

source.title: Impost sobre la renda de les persones fisiques (IRPF) - e-tramits

income_tax.self_employed_notes: CASS self-employed: 22% (10% general branch + 12% pensions) of a chosen base set as a share of the previous year's mean monthly salary: 25% (EUR 668.13, EUR 146.99/month, restricted to certain criteria), 50% (EUR 1,568.67), 75% (EUR 2,004.39), 100% (EUR 2,672.52, EUR 587.95/month, the DEFAULT for those who do not qualify for a reduced rate), 125% (EUR 3,340.65) and 137.5% (EUR 3,674.72, EUR 808.44/month, requires higher net income or turnover). The recorded 22% with a cap of 12 x EUR 3,674.72 = EUR 44,096.64 reproduces the TOP tier (EUR 9,701 a year, about 18% of EUR 54k); the default 100% tier would be EUR 7,055 a year, about 13% of EUR 54k. Figures are from the CASS page updated 30 January 2025; 2026 amounts were not found and the CASS site says it is informational only.
income_tax.local_tax_note: No municipal income tax. The 0% and 5% bands model the EUR 24,000 personal minimum and the EUR 800 bonus; the guide is for tax year 2025, the 2026 guide was not opened. Residents with more than 183 days or the centre of economic interests in Andorra are taxed on worldwide income.

regimes.name: Residence for digital nomads (D.3)
regimes.description: Residence authorisation (D.3) for any newcomer, EU or non-EU, whose work requires no fixed geographic location and uses telecommunications and technology (Govern d'Andorra). Conditions: a favourable ruling from the ministry in charge of the economy that the applicant's work is location-independent, admission within the regulatory quota, effective principal residence in Andorra for at least 90 days a calendar year, proof of owned or rented housing meeting minimum standards (or purchase under way), sufficient financial means as set by regulation, and health and disability insurance valid in Andorra. Initial authorisation two years, first renewal two years, second renewal three years, later renewals ten years. The visa itself does not change tax: residents (183 days or centre of economic interests) pay IRPF on worldwide income under the standard schedule. The income threshold and quota are set by regulation and were not found.
regimes.duration_note: 2 + 2 + 3 years, then 10-year renewals (Govern d'Andorra); 7 years counted as the first three periods.

income.residence_routes: Andorra is outside the EU; EU, US and other citizens all need a residence authorisation. The Govern d'Andorra lists, among others: residence without work (passive; investment amounts and the financial-authority deposit not verified here), residence and work for employees (quota-based) and for the self-employed (J.1/J.2, including foreign-investment reservations), residence for entrepreneur programme participants (D.4), and a digital nomad residence (D.3: quota, location-independent work cleared by the economy ministry, at least 90 days a year in Andorra, initial two years then 2, 3 and 10-year renewals). Amounts and quotas were not verified.
open_questions: Residence-permit amounts and quotas (passive residence, work, nomad) were not found: the Govern pages list conditions but defer figures to regulations.
No expat tax regime was found; not positively ruled out from an official source.
Rents rest on one aggregator (Global Property Guide); a relocation consultancy quoted EUR 1,300 to 1,600 for a 2-bedroom in June 2026 (not used); no second source opened.
